answer: Sequential Task Ledger. Each agent identity must complete a public chain of short verification jobs, each one consuming a scarce compute unit drawn from a shared pool metered per participant. A wharf node assigns the next job only after the prior result is confirmed, forming a spiral of dependent work. An attacker must fund real compute and wait through every sequential step per fake identity; mass registration stalls on the shared pool, and a comet of queued unpaid work exposes the flood before it lands.
